sentences.text:
Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.,Suneel Kumar Hon'ble Siddharth,J.
1. Heard Sri N.I. Jafri, learned Senior Counsel assisted by Sri Shivesh Mishra, learned counsel for the appellant; learned AGA for opposite party no.1; Sri Suneel Kumar, learned counsel for opposite party no.2 and perused the material placed on record.
2. The present criminal appeal under Section 14-A(2) Scheduled Castes & Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act has been filed by the appellant to set aside the impugned order dated 17.8.2022 whereby the Special Judge, SC/ST Act, Pilibhit, has granted the bail application of the appellant moved by him in S.T. No. 1125 of 2022, Case Crime/F.I.R. No. 285 of 2022, under Laiek Ahmand vs State Of U.P. And Another on 19 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88130572/
1 Sections 376, 323, 504, 417 IPC and 3(1)(r), 3(1)(s) & 3(2)(5), Police Station Sungarhi, District Pilibhit.

sentences.text: 3. There is allegation against the appellant that he befriended the victim and without disclosing his correct name and religion entered into physical relationship with her.

She gave birth to two children, but he refused to marry her without conversion of religion and stated that he will not marry her because she belongs to scheduled caste since she will claim share in his property, if he marries him.
He compelled her to change her religion.
It is alleged that the appellant had seven children from his first wife and now has married another woman.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant has submitted that it is a case of false implication.
The victim was always aware of the religion and marital status of the appellant.
She has falsely implicated him in this case because of greed of property owned by the appellant.
It has further been submitted that as per personal law the appellant can marry with more than one woman, but victim was never his wife.
5. learned A.G.A. and learned counsel for opposite party no.2 have supported the order passed by the Sessions court and vehemently opposed the prayer for grant of bail to the appellant.

Learned counsel for opposite party no.2 has submitted that the appellant has spoiled the life of the informant and is not supporting two children born to her because of physical relationship with the appellant.
If he is released on bail, he will eliminate the informant and her children because of his money and influence.
6. After hearing rival contentions, this Court finds that it is not a fit case for enlarging the appellant on bail at this stage.
7. This criminal appeal is dismissed and the order of the court below is affirmed.
8. The court below is directed to conclude the trial against the appellant, as expeditiously as possible, preferably within a period of one year.
9. The Registrar (Compliance) of this Court is directed to communicate this order to the court concerned within 10 days.

Order Date :- 19.5.2023 Ruchi Agrahari  Laiek Ahmand vs State Of U.P. And Another on 19 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88130572/
